sources.cite: Consumer face-shape heuristics (qualitative; widely repeated in beauty guides, no single primary source)
sources.note: Jaw widest, forehead narrowest. Qualitative -> numeric by us: jaw_to_mid 1.00 (jaw as wide as the cheeks), upper_to_mid 0.80 (narrow), chin_taper 0.60 (broad chin). width_length_ratio 0.70 is a neutral middle: the heuristic says nothing about length.

sources.cite: Consumer face-shape heuristics (qualitative; widely repeated in beauty guides, no single primary source)
sources.note: Cheekbones widest, forehead and jaw both narrow, pointed chin. Qualitative -> numeric by us: upper_to_mid 0.80, jaw_to_mid 0.75, chin_taper 0.40; width_length_ratio 0.70 neutral. Spreads and weights: see classes.Triangle.prototype source.

sources.cite: Consumer face-shape heuristics (qualitative; widely repeated in beauty guides, no single primary source)
sources.note: Forehead widest, narrow jaw, pointed chin. Qualitative -> numeric by us: upper_to_mid 1.00, jaw_to_mid 0.75, chin_taper 0.35; width_length_ratio 0.70 neutral. Spreads and weights: see classes.Triangle.prototype source.

sources.cite: Consumer face-shape heuristics (qualitative; widely repeated in beauty guides, no single primary source)
sources.note: Forehead widest, jaw narrowing to a less pointed chin than Heart. Qualitative -> numeric by us: upper_to_mid 1.00, jaw_to_mid 0.80, chin_taper 0.50; width_length_ratio 0.70 neutral. Spreads and weights: see classes.Triangle.prototype source.

sources.cite: Consumer face-shape heuristics (qualitative; widely repeated in beauty guides, no single primary source)
sources.note: Clearly longer than 1.5x the width; forehead, cheeks and jaw similar. Qualitative -> numeric by us: width_length_ratio 0.60, upper_to_mid 1.00, jaw_to_mid 1.00, chin_taper 0.50. Spreads and weights: see classes.Triangle.prototype source.

sources.cite: Consumer face-shape heuristics (qualitative; widely repeated in beauty guides, no single primary source)
sources.note: Length about 1.5x width (width_length_ratio 0.67 = 1/1.5, the one ratio these guides state numerically), forehead slightly wider than a rounded jaw. Qualitative -> numeric by us: upper_to_mid 0.90, jaw_to_mid 0.85, chin_taper 0.45. KNOWN BIAS: the guides measure hairline to chin; face_length_mesh stops at mesh point 10, below the hairline, so our width_length_ratio reads higher than theirs and this seed will lean towards Round and Square until calibrated. Spreads and weights: see classes.Triangle.prototype source.

sources.cite: Consumer face-shape heuristics (qualitative; widely repeated in beauty guides, no single primary source)

sources.cite: Consumer face-shape heuristics (qualitative; widely repeated in beauty guides, no single primary source)

sources.cite: Rule of fifths (neoclassical facial canon; the face is five eye-widths wide)
sources.note: Centre 0.20 = one fifth. The +/-0.02 Average band is a placeholder pending benchmark (no source). Canons are not ideals (spec: Research basis); used only to place the Average band.

sources.cite: Consumer eye-shape heuristic: upturned = outer corner above the inner corner, downturned = below
sources.note: Centre 0 deg is the heuristic's own definition. The +/-3 deg Average band is a placeholder pending benchmark (no source); the fixture face's noise band for canthal_tilt_deg is about +/-6 deg (bands are conservative by construction), so expect boundaryUncertain often.

sources.cite: Farkas et al. 1985 neoclassical canon (intercanthal width = eye fissure width); consumer rule 'eyes one eye-width apart'
sources.note: Centre 1.0 from the canon. The +/-0.1 Average band is a placeholder pending benchmark (no source).

sources.cite: placeholder pending benchmark (no source)
sources.note: Only the ORDER is from consumer heuristics (Round = tallest opening, Narrow = flattest, Almond between). Thresholds eye_aperture_ratio > 0.33 Round and < 0.22 Narrow have no source.

sources.cite: placeholder pending benchmark (no source)
sources.note: Only the qualitative definitions are consumer heuristics (Straight = little arch; angled = a peak with a dropping tail; Rounded = curved, no sharp peak). Thresholds brow_arch_ratio < 0.08, brow_tail_tilt_deg > 35 (Hard Angled) and > 20 (Soft Angled) have no source. Perfect Corp's 'Obscured' is not a label here: hidden brows are not_assessable.

sources.cite: Consumer brow-mapping rule: the brow starts above the inner eye corner
sources.note: interbrow_ratio 1.0 = brow heads exactly above the inner corners. The +/-0.1 Average band is a placeholder pending benchmark (no source).

sources.cite: Consumer brow-mapping rule: the brow runs from above the inner eye corner to the line from the nostril through the outer eye corner
sources.note: A brow that follows the rule is at least as long as the eye, so brow_length_to_eye_ratio < 1.0 is Short. Derived by us from a qualitative rule; unvalidated.

sources.cite: placeholder pending benchmark (no source)
sources.note: Heavy Upper Lip at upper_lower_lip_ratio > 1.0 follows from the words (upper lip taller than lower). Every other lipShape threshold (tilt > 5 deg, ratio < 0.5, fullness > 0.45 / > 0.5 / < 0.3, bow depth > 0.05) and the rule order have no source.

sources.cite: Farkas et al. 1985 neoclassical canon (mouth width = 1.5 x nasal width)
sources.note: alar_width_to_mouth_ratio 0.667 = 1/1.5 centres Wide (< 0.60) and Narrow (> 0.75); the band edges are placeholders pending benchmark. The measurement uses the nostril-base points (ALAR_BASE, mesh 98/327), a proxy for alare (proxy: true), so the canon centre is applied to a proxy of the width it defines.

sources.cite: Farkas et al. 1985 neoclassical canon (nasal width = intercanthal width)
sources.note: Centre 1.0 from the canon. The +/-0.1 Average band is a placeholder pending benchmark (no source). alar_width_to_intercanthal_ratio uses the nostril-base points (ALAR_BASE, mesh 98/327), a proxy for alare (proxy: true), so the canon centre is applied to a proxy of the width it defines.

sources.cite: Equal facial thirds canon (Jayaratne et al. 2012 found it met in 0% of 103 adults: a heuristic midpoint, not a norm)
sources.note: Equal middle and lower thirds give nose_length_ratio 0.5. The +/-0.03 Average band is a placeholder pending benchmark (no source).
